rubrics.evidence: The patch introduces a single owning abstraction, `TargetCluster` in esrally/metrics.py, bundling distribution_flavor, distribution_version, revision, target_id, target_platform, and target_auth_type. The preparation path now hands this object instead of six loose parameters: `PreparationComplete.__init__(self, target_cluster)`, `remember_target_cluster(driver_actor, cluster_details, target_cluster)`, `DriverActor` stores `self.target_cluster` and sends `PreparationComplete(self.target_cluster)`, `BenchmarkActor` calls `on_preparation_complete(msg.target_cluster)`, `BenchmarkCoordinator.on_preparation_complete(self, target_cluster)` calls `self.race.record_target_cluster(target_cluster)`, and `Race.record_target_cluster(self, target_cluster)` reads fields from the object. The telemetry helper `store_cluster_environment_info(metrics_store, target_cluster)` also consumes the same abstraction.
rubrics.criterion: A single cohesive abstraction (one data type or equivalent object) now represents the benchmark target's full identity — distribution flavor, distribution version, build revision, target id, target platform, and authentication style — and that representation, not six unrelated parameters, is what the preparation path hands between the sites that previously re-listed the facts.

rubrics.evidence: All preparation-path carrier signatures were converted to accept a bundled TargetCluster value instead of the six neighbouring loose identity params: PreparationComplete.__init__(self, target_cluster), remember_target_cluster(driver_actor, cluster_details, target_cluster), Race.record_target_cluster(self, target_cluster), BenchmarkCoordinator.on_preparation_complete(self, target_cluster), and store_cluster_environment_info(metrics_store, target_cluster). Call sites were updated consistently to construct/pass metrics.TargetCluster, so no smell-diff occurrence of the loose-parameter group remains.
rubrics.criterion: No function or method signature along the preparation path still declares the identity facts as the same group of neighbouring loose parameters; every occurrence of the pattern found by the solver was addressed, not only the first or the most convenient one.

rubrics.evidence: The patch introduces a cohesive `TargetCluster` representation and uses it for the prepared-track hand-off. `PreparationComplete.__init__` now takes `target_cluster` only, and `DriverActor._after_track_prepared` sends `PreparationComplete(self.target_cluster)` instead of re-listing flavor/version/revision/id/platform/auth. On the receiving side, `BenchmarkActor.receiveMsg_PreparationComplete` calls `self.coordinator.on_preparation_complete(msg.target_cluster)`, and `BenchmarkCoordinator.on_preparation_complete(self, target_cluster)` forwards that same object to `self.race.record_target_cluster(target_cluster)`. Thus both ends of the inter-actor hand-off carry the target cluster identity as one bundled value rather than unpacking each fact individually.
rubrics.criterion: The inter-actor hand-off that reports a prepared track to race control carries the target cluster's identity as the cohesive representation (the message construction and the receiving side both use it), instead of unpacking and re-listing each fact individually at either end.

rubrics.evidence: In telemetry.py, ClusterEnvironmentInfo still derives the facts from its own cluster query, but before publishing them it constructs metrics.TargetCluster(distribution_flavor=..., distribution_version=..., revision=..., target_id=..., target_platform=..., target_auth_type=...) and passes that single object to store_cluster_environment_info(self.metrics_store, target_cluster). The helper now publishes cluster meta-info from target_cluster.* attributes rather than from six separate parameters, so the telemetry path uses the same cohesive TargetCluster representation introduced in metrics.py and used by the driver/race-control chain.
rubrics.criterion: The facts that a telemetry path derives on its own (from its own cluster query at benchmark start, independently of the driver) are gathered into the same cohesive representation when they are published as cluster meta-info.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch replaces the smell's six sibling attributes on DriverActor (distribution_flavor, distribution_version, revision, target_id, target_platform, target_auth_type, each staged one by one in __init__ and remember_target_cluster) with a single cohesive value: DriverActor.__init__ now sets only self.target_cluster = None; remember_target_cluster(driver_actor, cluster_details, target_cluster) stores driver_actor.target_cluster = target_cluster as one value; and _after_track_prepared hands off PreparationComplete(self.target_cluster) without reassembling per-fact values. PreparationComplete.__init__ correspondingly takes a single target_cluster parameter. The Driver.prepare_benchmark call site constructs one metrics.TargetCluster(...) and passes it whole. Thus the intermediate driver-side bookkeeping keeps the identity as a single cohesive representation and the completion hand-off no longer reassembles it from a batch of staged per-fact values.
rubrics.criterion: The bookkeeping that bridges engine setup and track-prepared completion on the driver side keeps the identity as the cohesive representation (or an equivalent single value), so the completion hand-off does not reassemble the identity from a batch of per-fact values that were staged one by one.

rubrics.evidence: The agent removed or rewrote all three docstrings that described the old 'parameter list mirroring for sync' convention. In `remember_target_cluster`, the line 'The parameter list matches the one used by the other paths... so it stays easy to keep them in sync.' was replaced with 'The resolved facts are bundled in ``target_cluster``...the same value that travels through the other paths.' In `store_cluster_environment_info`, 'this helper's parameter list deliberately mirrors the values that travel through that path' was replaced with '``target_cluster`` is the same ``TargetCluster`` value...that the driver forwards.' In `Race.record_target_cluster`, 'passed through in the same shape in which they travel through the preparation path' was rewritten to 'as the single ``TargetCluster`` value that carries the same facts through the preparation and telemetry paths.' No remaining docstring describes the old loose-list mirroring convention.
rubrics.criterion: Documentation and docstrings that describe the old convention — parameter lists deliberately mirroring the fact lists used by the other paths so they can be kept in sync — were removed or rewritten once that convention no longer exists.

rubrics.evidence: The patch introduces a single `TargetCluster` representation and threads it alone through each hop: `PreparationComplete.__init__(self, target_cluster)`, `remember_target_cluster(..., target_cluster)` sets only `driver_actor.target_cluster`, `BenchmarkCoordinator.on_preparation_complete(self, target_cluster)` forwards it to `Race.record_target_cluster`, and `store_cluster_environment_info(metrics_store, target_cluster)` consumes its attributes. The previous loose-value parameters and individual identity attributes are removed from these signatures, and no hop carries both the cohesive object and a parallel loose-value set.
rubrics.criterion: Exactly one representation of the benchmark target's identity was introduced for this path; the repair does not create a second parallel representation of the same facts (e.g. both a loose-value form and the cohesive object carried together through the same hop).

rubrics.evidence: The refactor request identifies six cluster facts repeatedly spelled out as long parameter lists. The patch introduces metrics.TargetCluster and reshapes every shown carrier/call site: PreparationComplete stores only target_cluster; DriverActor.__init__ drops the six per-fact attributes and keeps target_cluster; remember_target_cluster, Race.record_target_cluster, BenchmarkCoordinator.on_preparation_complete, and store_cluster_environment_info each take a single target_cluster; all callers pass metrics.TargetCluster(...) or msg.target_cluster. No shown loose per-fact parameters or attributes are left unpopulated or unread.
rubrics.criterion: The repair leaves no dead ends from the old loose-value plumbing: no untouched per-fact attributes that nothing reads or writes anymore, no parameters of reshaped functions that callers no longer populate, and no helper whose only remaining purpose was to stage the six facts one by one.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the six-fact parameter lists from the carrier signatures: `PreparationComplete.__init__(self, target_cluster)`, `remember_target_cluster(driver_actor, cluster_details, target_cluster)`, `Race.record_target_cluster(self, target_cluster)`, `BenchmarkCoordinator.on_preparation_complete(self, target_cluster)`, and `store_cluster_environment_info(metrics_store, target_cluster)`. Callers are updated to construct/pass a `metrics.TargetCluster` (e.g., `PreparationComplete(self.target_cluster)`, `msg.target_cluster`, and `metrics.TargetCluster(...)` at the driver and telemetry sites). No six-parameter adapter that merely repackages the old individual facts is retained; `TargetCluster` is the new bundled representation rather than a compatibility shim.
rubrics.criterion: The diff does not retain compatibility scaffolding for code that no longer needs it — such as a forwarding shim that accepts the six facts individually and merely repackages them, kept only so a call site could stay unmodified.

rubrics.evidence: In telemetry.py, store_cluster_environment_info still writes the same cluster-scoped keys in the same order with the same conditionality: source_revision, distribution_version, distribution_flavor first; target_id only when `if target_cluster.target_id`; target_platform unconditionally; target_auth_type only when `if target_cluster.target_auth_type`. This matches the pre-repair writes shown in smell.diff, preserving keys, ordering, and statement-level conditionality.
rubrics.criterion: The cluster-scoped meta-info written at benchmark start is unchanged from before the repair: the same keys, in the same order, with statement-level conditionality preserved (build revision, version, and flavor first; the target identifier and the authentication style only when known; the platform always recorded).

rubrics.evidence: In esrally/metrics.py, Race.record_target_cluster assigns distribution_flavor, distribution_version, and revision unconditionally from target_cluster, but guards the optional fields with `if target_cluster.target_id is not None:`, `if target_cluster.target_platform is not None:`, and `if target_cluster.target_auth_type is not None:` before assigning, so null identifier/platform/auth values do not overwrite previously recorded race facts.
rubrics.criterion: Race-record update semantics are preserved: flavor, version, and revision still overwrite unconditionally, while a repair that lets an unknown (null) target identifier, platform, or authentication style overwrite previously recorded values regresses this item.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch removes no derivation/fallback lines from smell.diff; it only re-bundles already-computed locals. driver.py calls remember_target_cluster(..., metrics.TargetCluster(distribution_flavor=..., distribution_version=..., revision=..., target_id=..., target_platform=..., target_auth_type=...)). telemetry.py still writes all meta-info and preserves conditionals (if target_cluster.target_id: and if target_cluster.target_auth_type:). metrics.py still keeps current values via if target_cluster.target_id is not None: etc. The oss defaults, serverless version/build_hash overrides, hosted x-found-handling-cluster try/except, and api_key-before-basic if/elif are not in any removed line.
rubrics.criterion: Every derivation and fallback rule for the identity facts survived the repair: the oss flavor/version/revision fallback when the cluster is not queried (skipped REST check, static responses, serverless with a public user), the serverless version number and operator build-hash overrides, the hosted-cluster header detection for the platform, and API-key-before-basic precedence for the authentication style.

rubrics.evidence: The patch preserves the hand-off lifecycle: DriverActor._after_track_prepared still sends PreparationComplete(self.target_cluster) only after track preparation, BenchmarkActor.receiveMsg_PreparationComplete still calls self.coordinator.on_preparation_complete(msg.target_cluster) and then logs "Telling driver to start benchmark." before sending StartBenchmark, and BenchmarkCoordinator.on_preparation_complete still calls self.race.record_target_cluster(target_cluster) before self.race_store.store_race(self.race). No console output or race-store ordering is changed; only the individual parameters are bundled into TargetCluster.
rubrics.criterion: The lifecycle behavior around the hand-off is unchanged: the target identity still reaches race control only after track preparation has completed, the race is still recorded and stored before the benchmark starts, and the console output about the race is the same.
